name: Telescope Array

facility_roles.note: The facility and the experiment coincide: the Telescope Array observatory hosts and is the detector for this experiment.

intervals.label: data taking (original array)
intervals.quote: 16 years of data collected from 11 May 2008 to 10 May 2024
intervals.note: 10 May 2024 is the end of a 16-year analysis dataset window used in a 2026 paper, not a stated end of operations; no fetched source says the array has stopped taking data. No fetched source in this session gives a construction-start date distinct from this first-data date.

intervals.label: TAx4 extension data taking
intervals.quote: three years of data collected from October 2019 to September 2022
intervals.note: TAx4 expands the original TA aperture by a factor of four (~3000 km^2 target), adding 500 SDs on a 2.08 km grid and 12 new FD telescopes. September 2022 is the end of an analysis dataset window, not a stated end of TAx4 operations.

physics_goals.value: Determine the origin, composition and acceleration mechanism of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays using a hybrid surface-detector and fluorescence-telescope array in the Northern Hemisphere.
physics_goals.quote: The Telescope Array (TA) experiment is a hybrid UHECR observatory in the Northern Hemisphere located near Delta, Utah, USA

unique_capabilities.value: The largest ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory in the Northern Hemisphere, complementing the Pierre Auger Observatory's Southern Hemisphere sky coverage; extended fourfold in area by the TAx4 project to gain statistics at the very highest energies.
unique_capabilities.quote: the TA×4 project expands the original TA aperture by a factor of four, with a target coverage of ~3000 km^2

quantity.quote: covering an area of about 700 km^2
507 plastic scintillation counters deployed on a 1.2 km square grid
a total of 38 telescopes for hybrid measurements
with a target coverage of ~3000 km^2

summary.plain: A cosmic-ray observatory in the Utah desert with over 500 ground detectors spread across 700 square kilometres and telescopes at three stations, watching for the rarest, most energetic particles from space; recently made four times bigger by the TAx4 extension.
summary.technical: Hybrid ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray observatory near Delta, Utah (~1400 m altitude): 507 plastic-scintillator surface-detector stations on a 1.2 km grid over ~700 km^2, plus 38 fluorescence telescopes at three sites (Middle Drum, Long Ridge, Black Rock Mesa). Taking data since 11 May 2008; extended since October 2019 by TAx4 (500 additional SDs on a 2.08 km grid, 12 new FD telescopes, target ~3000 km^2).
